chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Ishaq Thalabah ibn Maymun, from a man who had named him, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The most truthful of the names are those named by servitude (to Allah), and the best of them are the names of the Prophets.

key_terms.أَصْدَقُ الْأَسْمَاءِ: The most truthful of the names
key_terms.الْعُبُودِيَّةِ: Servitude or slavery to God, indicating truthfulness in naming

ai.seo_question: What are considered the most truthful and best names in Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a hierarchy of nomenclature, identifying names denoting 'servitude' (Abd) as the most truthful because they reflect the fundamental human purpose of worship. He further elevates the names of the Prophets as the most excellent, linking personal identity to prophetic legacy. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on 'Ubudiyyah (servitude to God) as the core of spiritual authenticity and social identity.
